discovery: Discovery of multiband superconductivity in magnesium diboride and the iron-based superconductors

nominees.name: Hideo Hosono
nominees.affiliation: Tokyo Institute of Technology (Institute of Science Tokyo), Japan

nominees.name: Jun Akimitsu
nominees.affiliation: Okayama University / Aoyama Gakuin University, Japan

nominees.name: Zhongxian Zhao
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China

motivation: Akimitsu's 2001 discovery of 39 K superconductivity in MgB2 and Hosono's 2008 discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides, driven to 55 K by Zhao's group, broke the long-held view that superconductivity is described by a single order parameter, with cuprates the lone high-temperature exception. These materials revealed that several electronic bands can condense into coupled, distinct gaps, a genuinely new organising principle. The consequences reach far beyond higher transition temperatures: multiband condensates exhibit phenomena impossible in single-component systems, including fractional-flux vortices, intermediate type-1.5 magnetic response, s+- pairing, nematicity and time-reversal-symmetry-breaking states, many now confirmed by direct imaging and thermodynamic experiments. MgB2 is also a practical conductor for magnets and cables. These discoveries opened two entire material families, founded a field of thousands of researchers, and permanently rewrote the textbook picture of the superconducting state.
